quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The best protection when riding a motorcycle is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to stay far away from other vehicles. Distance gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper protective gear is also important.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce engine speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce engine speed.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly reduce engine speed. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always on the right side of the lane.
Is always in the center of the lane.
Is always on the left side of the lane.
Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. You should change your position in the lane as road, weather, and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Drivers entering from an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility.
Move to a different lane, away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Weave in your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane, away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them more space.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Can take corners at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar motorcycle can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is just as good as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Should only be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not an adequate replacement for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not fully protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may show:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limits.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most crashes happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Always be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, your motorcycle must have all of the following, except:

options.text: A seat big enough for two people.
Working lights, mirrors, and good tires.
A sign on the back saying a passenger is riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sign on the back saying a passenger is riding.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle needs a seat for two people and foot pegs for the passenger. You must also adjust your motorcycle for the extra weight. No sign is required.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face in a crash.
Is only useful for protection from dirt.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: If you are not going slowly enough when shifting to a lower gear, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could speed up too fast.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, check everything except the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, inspect your motorcycle thoroughly. Check the tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not depend on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle but do not consciously notice it.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: To lean the motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. To turn, press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, ride with your headlight on and choose a lane position that lets oncoming traffic see you. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can avoid hazards. Do not rely on eye contact with drivers to make them notice you.

questions.question: The best sitting position when riding:

options.text: Requires your arms to hold you up.
Lets you easily reach the controls.
Keeps your arms straight when holding the handgrips.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. You should not have to stretch to reach the handgrips. Your arms should bend slightly when holding them. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This allows experienced riders at the back to watch them.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep going straight. If you need to brake, slowly apply brake pressure to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Long rides in cold weather can cause all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you easier to see.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
questions.explanation: Slow down before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: If a dog chases you, you should:

options.text: Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If chased, downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.
